234		var tooMany *TooManyRedirectsError

243	// where it pointed, whether that was the URL it built or somewhere a redirect

247		// redacted where the message is built. Holding the raw value and redacting
248		// at the one place it renders is what makes redaction a property of the type
249		// rather than a step every caller constructing one has to remember.

255	}

258	// does.

260		return fmt.Sprintf(

269	type TooManyRedirectsError struct {
270		// URL is where the chain started, held raw and redacted where it renders.
271		URL string
272	
273		// Limit is the number of redirects harnaas followed before stopping.
274		Limit int
275	}
276	
277	// Error states the problem and then the fix.
278	func (e *TooManyRedirectsError) Error() string {
279		return fmt.Sprintf(
280			"fetching %s followed %d redirects without arriving\n\n"+
281				"The host is redirecting in a loop or through more hops than harnaas follows. "+
282				"Check that the manifest names the repository directly rather than a URL that forwards to it.",
283			RedactURL(e.URL), e.Limit,
284		)
285	}
286	
287	// ResponseTooLargeError reports a body past the size ceiling.
288	type ResponseTooLargeError struct {
289		// URL is the destination that served it, held raw and redacted where it
290		// renders.
291		URL string
292	
293		// Limit is the ceiling in bytes, so the message states the number the
294		// response has to come under rather than only that it did not.
295		Limit int64
296	}
297	
298	// Error states the problem and then the fix.
299	func (e *ResponseTooLargeError) Error() string {

301			"%s served more than the %d bytes harnaas reads from one source\n\n"+
302				"Harness assets are documents, so a source this large is nearly always a repository that happens to contain them rather than the repository they live in. "+
303				"Declare a source that holds the assets themselves.",
304			RedactURL(e.URL), e.Limit,
305		)
306	}

308	// StatusError reports a response harnaas will not read.
309	//
310	// It is deliberately a plain transport diagnostic: the kind that made the request
311	// is the only thing that knows which asset, repository and commit the URL stood
312	// for, so it is what turns a 404 into a message about a missing path.
313	type StatusError struct {
314		// URL is the destination, held raw and redacted where it renders.
315		URL string
316	
317		// StatusCode is the response status, kept as a number so a caller can
318		// recognize the cases it has something better to say about.
319		StatusCode int
320	
321		// Status is the status line, which carries the host's own wording.
322		Status string
323	}
324

328			"%s answered %s\n\n"+
329				"Check that the source the manifest declares exists and is readable, then run harnaas install again.",
330			RedactURL(e.URL), e.Status,
331		)
332	}

334	// FetchError reports a request that produced no usable response at all.
335	type FetchError struct {
336		// URL is the destination, held raw and redacted where it renders.
337		URL string
338	
339		// Err is the underlying failure, kept so a caller can recognize a cancelled
340		// run through errors.Is.
341		Err error
342	}
343	
344	// Error states the problem and then the fix.
345	//

347	// restates the URL unredacted, so quoting it would put back exactly what
348	// [RedactURL] exists to remove — and it adds nothing, since the destination is
349	// already the first thing this message names.
350	func (e *FetchError) Error() string {
351		cause := e.Err
352	
353		var wrapped *url.Error
354		if errors.As(cause, &wrapped) {
355			cause = wrapped.Err
356		}
357	
358		return fmt.Sprintf(
359			"could not fetch %s: %s\n\n"+
360				"Check that this machine can reach the host, then run harnaas install again.",
361			RedactURL(e.URL), cause,
362		)
363	}
364	
365	// Unwrap keeps the cause reachable, so a fetch ended by an interrupt is still
366	// recognizable as a cancelled context rather than as a network failure.
367	func (e *FetchError) Unwrap() error { return e.Err }

8	// Content arrives as one archive per repository and commit, never as one request

10	// a listing plus a request per file against a budget a CI job installing a
11	// handful of assets exhausts — and would give the cache a set of files to
12	// reconcile instead of one immutable object named by the commit it is of.
13	//
14	// The consequence is this file: several assets legitimately name different
15	// subtrees of one repository at one commit, so retrieval has to be asked for per
16	// asset and performed once. The memory of what has already been fetched is per
17	// run, which is why the source contract registers a constructor rather than a
18	// value — a memo shared between runs would either leak content into a later one
19	// or need a global to hold it.
20	
21	// archiveHost is the endpoint archives are fetched from, and the only place its
22	// name is spelled.
23	//
24	// It is the API's tarball endpoint rather than the content host directly,
25	// because that is the documented route that takes an authorization header — the
26	// one a private repository needs, and the reason the fetcher follows a bounded
27	// redirect chain: the endpoint answers with a signed URL on the content host,
28	// whose query string carries the grant that [source.RedactURL] exists to drop.
29	const archiveHost = "api.github.com"
30	
31	// archiveURL is the archive of one repository at one commit.
32	//
33	// The commit is used rather than the ref the manifest declared, so the URL names
34	// an object that cannot change under it — which is what makes the response
35	// content-addressable and the same archive reusable for every asset that
36	// resolved to it.
37	func archiveURL(repository, commit string) string {
38		return "https://" + archiveHost + "/repos/" + repository + "/tarball/" + commit

42	//
43	// It is a parameter rather than a call for the reason [gitRunner] is: a
44	// resolution has to be exercisable without a network, and the fetcher's own
45	// rules — https only, no destination on this machine — mean a test server cannot
46	// stand in for the forge. The production value is [source.Fetcher.Fetch], which
47	// is the only way harnaas makes an HTTP request at all.
48	type archiveFetcher func(ctx context.Context, url string) ([]byte, error)
49	
50	// archiveKey identifies one archive: a repository and the commit its content is
51	// of.
52	//
53	// The commit and not the ref, because two assets pinned to `v1.2.0` and to the
54	// commit that tag names are the same fetch, and the ref is what resolution has
55	// already spent.
56	type archiveKey struct {
57		repository string
58		commit     string
59	}
60	
61	// archives is one run's memory of the archives it has retrieved.
62	type archives struct {
63		fetch archiveFetcher
64	
65		// mu guards fetched, and is held only while the slot for a key is found or
66		// created — never across the retrieval itself, so one repository's fetch
67		// does not queue behind another's.
68		mu      sync.Mutex
69		fetched map[archiveKey]*fetchedArchive
70	}

78	// most once, and whatever it produced.

81		body []byte
82		err  error

89	// asset referencing the same repository would meet the same host and the same
90	// answer, so asking again would multiply one outage by the number of assets
91	// declared against it — and the caller attributes the remembered failure to its
92	// own asset, so the second asset's diagnostic still names the second asset.

106		})
107	
108		return entry.body, entry.err

21	// New returns the kind for one install run.
22	//

24	// only way harnaas makes an HTTP request — so every transport rule applies here
25	// by there being no second route to a request.
26	func New() source.Kind {
27		return newKind(runGit, source.NewFetcher().Fetch)
28	}

30	// newKind is [New] with the git invocation and the retrieval as parameters, so a
31	// whole resolution is exercisable with neither a network nor a repository.
32	func newKind(run gitRunner, fetch archiveFetcher) *Kind {
33		return &Kind{run: run, archives: newArchives(fetch)}
34	}

36	// Resolve produces one asset's content and provenance.
37	//
38	// The three steps are deliberately separate: the declared ref becomes a commit
39	// before anything is fetched, the commit's archive is retrieved at most once per
40	// run, and the subtree the asset names is taken out of it. Every failure is
41	// attributed to the asset, and none of them returns a resolved source — an empty
42	// one would converge to deleting every file the asset had installed, which is
43	// why [source.NewResolved] refuses one and why nothing here builds a [source.Resolved]
44	// by any other route.
45	func (k *Kind) Resolve(ctx context.Context, req source.Request) (*source.Resolved, error) {
46		resolution, err := resolveRef(ctx, k.run, remoteURL(req.Source.Repository), req)
47		if err != nil {
48			return nil, err
49		}
50	
51		archive, err := k.archives.get(ctx, req.Source.Repository, resolution.Commit)
52		if err != nil {
53			return nil, retrievalFailure(req, resolution.Commit, err)
54		}
55	
56		content, err := source.ExtractSubtree(archive, req.Asset.Ref.Path, source.ArchiveSubject{
57			AssetID: req.Asset.ID,

63		}

65		resolved, err := source.NewResolved(source.Provenance{
66			Kind:   manifest.SourceKindGitHub,
67			Source: req.Source.String(),

69			// "the installed files still match the commit" and "the tag now points
70			// somewhere else" are the two questions lint asks separately.

143	}

### A token is named by where it came from, never by what it is

`HARNAAS_GITHUB_TOKEN`, `GH_TOKEN`, `GITHUB_TOKEN`, in that order, and proceeds unauthenticated when

authenticates needs no harnaas-specific configuration, and the harnaas-specific name comes first so a
project that needs something the ambient token cannot read has somewhere to say so. A variable set to
nothing counts as unset, because a job that exports a token conditionally leaves an empty value
